script: On a small sandbar in India, a teenage boy named Jadav noticed something sad. Floods kept washing dead snakes onto the bare sand, because there were no trees to give them shade. So he planted one bamboo seed. Then another. Every single day, for years, he kept planting, quietly, patiently, without telling anyone. Decades passed. Slowly, the empty sandbar became a real forest, thick with trees, deer, tigers, and elephants that finally had somewhere safe to live. Forest officials only discovered it by accident, thinking a wildfire was raging. Instead they found a forest larger than many parks, grown entirely by one man's calm, steady hands. Today it's called Molai Forest, a quiet gift, planted one seed at a time.
